qAndA.question: What is the name of the space created by the descending genitalia during fetal development?
What are the two openings of the inguinal canal called?
What structure forms the inferior wall of the inguinal canal?
What two muscles contribute to both the superior and posterior walls of the canal?
What is the last layer separating the skin from the abdominal contents?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In the early stages of your life as a fetus, certain parts of your external genitalia were
inside your abdomen. As they pushed their way out, they created for themselves this space
that we now know as the Inguinal Canal. It's a space that begins a couple of centimetres
above the halfway point of the Inguinal ligament, which runs like this. To make it easier to
visualize, we've got it here as a rounded cubic prism. The two ends of the canal are called
the Inguinal Rings, superficial and deep. The contents of the canal are in males, the
spermatic cord, and in females, the round ligament. In both, there's the Iliot Inguinal Nerve as
well. So let's think about what holds these things in the canal, the walls that mark the
edges of the prism. The bottom wall is the easiest to remember. It's the Inguinal ligament we mentioned
before. The Asa or Anterior wall is also easy to remember. It's mostly made up of the
eponurosis of the external obliques. The external obliques is the most anterior muscle of the
abdominal wall. So you have the anterior wall of the Inguinal Canal made up by the most anterior
muscle. And interestingly, the Inguinal ligament is actually just an extension or a continuation of
this eponurosis. And further out, laterally, the anterior wall is reinforced by the next muscle of
the abdominal wall, internal obliques or I.O. For our purposes, this starts at the Iliot crest,
this bony prominence here. It moves that beside the external obliques and is joined here by the
next muscle of the abdominal wall, which begins further lateral on the Iliot crest. That's transversus
abdominis or TA. So I.O. and TA joined together to arch over the top. So what we imagine is the
superior wall of the Inguinal Canal is simply the part of these muscles which is flying free,
arching over the contents of the canal. They end up joining together to make the aptly named
con joint tendon, which inserts onto the pubic, chubicle down here. If we take a look around the
back now, you can see that the con joint tendon actually extends down over part of the posterior wall
of the Inguinal Canal. So I.O. and TA have made this journey from the Iliot crest, making up part
of the anterior wall, all of the superior wall, and then a little bit of the posterior wall of the
Inguinal Canal. And if we think about it, we've used up all of the abdominal wall muscles now to
make up the inferior, anterior, and superior wall. So what else is there between the skin and the
abdominal contents? What's going to hold the abdominal contents away from the contents of the
Inguinal Canal? So we've used up EO, I.O. and TA in that order from skin to abdominal cavity.
And the last layer isn't a muscle, it's a layer of fascia called the transversalist fascia.
It's the last thing we meet in terms of layers from the skin to the abdominal contents.
And interestingly, the deep Inguinal Ring is actually a hole in the transversalist fascia.
So now we've worked all that out, let's take a trip down the canal.
We'll hop through the deep ring first, which is the hole in the transversalist fascia.
We see right in front of us the muscle reinforcing the anterior wall of the Inguinal Canal.
That's internal obliques. And then to our right we see this other muscle that joins up with
internal obliques to arc over our heads and make up the superior wall.
And that's transversus abdominis.
Medially to them on the anterior wall is the uponurosis of the external obliques.
Keep cruising on down the canal now and we see the transversalist fascia on our left.
And then further down from that we see the end of the posterior wall made up by the con joint tendon,
which of course is the joint tenderness insertion of I-O and TA.
The floor is the Inguinal ligament, which is just an extension of the external obliques upon
your osus. And then lastly to our right we see a hole in the external obliques upon your osus,
the superficial Inguinal ring. So through this hole we go and if it's a male we're in,
we hop out that ring and land in the scrotum. And if it's a female we'll end up in the labia majora.
All right so there you go. I hope you enjoyed that little journey through the Inguinal Canal.
Thanks for watching, hit subscribe and we'll see you next time.
